page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics are relatively low, with stress-ng single-core performance and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show weak to poor performance. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 654.2 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 75.3 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-threaded capabilities, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extreme single-thread compute speeds. It is well-suited for database operations, as reflected in its average Passmark database and Redis SET performance. Other appropriate workloads include static web serving, software compilation, and light LLM inference using smaller models, whereas heavy single-threaded tasks or large-scale model inference are constrained by the hardware's single-core performance profile.
